newsitem.title: INDIA: Party rebels seek Yadav resignation over scandal.
newsitem.headline: Party rebels seek Yadav resignation over scandal.

text.p: The president of Indian Prime Minister Inder Kumar Gujral's Janata Dal party is facing pressure from party rebels to resign as the chief minister of the state of Bihar over a $280-million corruption scandal.

Party politicians say that Ramai Ram, a former state president of the party, is camping in Delhi to persuade national leaders to force the resignation of Laloo Prasad Yadav over the "fodder" scandal involving alleged illegal siphoning off of animal welfare funds.

More than 20 state-level lawmakers have backed calls for Yadav to quit in order to save the Janata Dal's image after federal police said last month that they had decided to prosecute him in the 10-billion rupee ($280 million) scandal.
Yadav, who has rejected calls that he must resign, says he is innocent in the scandal, which dates back to the mid-1980s.
"The party cannot be allowed to be the personal property of an individual as it is clear that corruption is not acceptable to the masses," a dissident leader told Reuters in Patna, the state capital.
The scandal broke out last year when officials discovered excessive withdrawals from animal welfare accounts.
The Central Bureau of Investigation (CBI) has sought permission from the state governor to prosecute Yadav, who is among 55 officials and politicians named by the CBI.
The governor says he needs time to examine a proposed chargesheet. Yadav has turned down demands that he must resign and face trial.

Police took more than 2,000 people into preventive custody on May 3 during a general strike called by the Hindu nationalist Bharatiya Janata Party (BJP) to press for Yadav's arrest. Normal life was paralysed in the mineral-rich state.

"I will continue to be the chief minister as long as I enjoy the confidence and support of party leaders and electorate. I am not at the mercy of the BJP or the CBI and they have not made me the chief minister of Bihar," Yadav said last month.
